title: Pre-Analysis — Electronic Ballast and Diffuser Change for the Fluorescent Ceiling and Wall Wash Lighting

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Pre-analysis of a ballast and diffuser change against fluorescent tube life and flicker complaints, cancelled part way through when the cabin programme took the question over as part of a wider lighting decision.

sections.objective: Assess a proposal to change the electronic ballast and the prismatic diffuser on the fluorescent ceiling and wall wash lighting, raised against tube life and against a flicker complaint that the cabin crew reporting system had carried for two years. The pre-analysis was scoped to the lighting installation only, on the assumption that the change was a component substitution; the question of whether the fluorescent architecture should be kept at all was explicitly out of scope at the time the order was raised.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed before the work order was stopped. The part list figure for the ceiling and wall wash installation carries the ballast and the diffuser as a single configuration with no alternate, and both change, so the figure needs a post-change state rather than a substitution. The lighting installation task calls the diffuser retention detail by a dimension that the new item changes, which is a small correction but one that has to reach the operator with the bulletin. More significantly, the pack bay noise reduction work under way in the same period claims the same overhead access and the same ceiling panel removal, and the two would arrive at an aircraft within months of each other. That observation, together with a parallel enquiry into solid state lighting, was what caused the cabin programme to take the whole question over.
sections.next_steps: The work order is stopped rather than concluded. The analysis file, the flicker complaint record and the three findings were handed to the cabin programme, which is assessing a solid state replacement of the whole installation and will decide whether a ballast change is still worth making. No recommendation is issued from this order and no change is proposed to the modification dossier while the wider decision is open.

similarity_seeds: fluorescent tube life and flicker in a passenger cabin
overhead ceiling panel access shared between cabin retrofits

tasks.title: Review the lighting part list and installation content
Search other work claiming the same overhead access
Assess whether the fluorescent architecture should be retained

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries the ballast and the diffuser as one configuration with no alternate item. Both change together, so a substitution in place would leave no way to order for an unmodified aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a part list change request for a post-change configuration, held pending the wider decision.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task states the diffuser retention detail as a dimension rather than as a reference. The new diffuser changes it, and a technician following the current dimension will over-compress the retainer.
expected_findings.resolution: Correct the dimension and publish it with whichever bulletin eventually carries the change.

expected_findings.rationale: The pack bay noise work needs the same overhead ceiling panels removed in the same cabin section. Two cabin retrofits arriving within months of each other for one piece of access is the kind of overlap the cabin programme exists to resolve.
expected_findings.resolution: Hand the overlap to the cabin programme together with the rest of the file.

type_data.conclusion: Stopped rather than concluded. The wider question of whether the fluorescent installation should be retained at all was outside this order's scope, and the file was handed to the cabin programme with its findings.
